classification.habit: Small prostrate or spreading perennial herb
classification.habitat: Dry open grassland, scrub and sandy soils

identification.description: Small spreading herb with narrow leaves and characteristic funnel-shaped flowers.
identification.whole_plant: Low, prostrate to ascending herb forming mats.
identification.stem: Thin, trailing to ascending, often branched from base.
identification.leaf: Small narrow linear-lanceolate leaves, usually alternate.
identification.flower: Small funnel-shaped flowers, commonly pale blue to whitish depending on form.
identification.bark: Not applicable as a distinct drug character.

therapeutics.precautions: Botanical identity is important because several plants are marketed under Shankhapushpi.

reference_hubs: TDU Indian Medicinal Plants Database — Shlokas

major_constituents: Flavonoid and phenolic constituents reported in studies
phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Phytochemical profiles vary with botanical identity and extraction.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Convolvulus pluricaulis is traditionally described as a medhya drug and has been investigated experimentally for neuropharmacological properties; clinical conclusions require preparation-specific evidence.
modern_information.safety_notes: Confirm botanical identity before using commercial Shankhapushpi preparations.

exam_points: Prostrate habit and funnel-shaped flowers are useful identification clues
viva_questions: Why is botanical authentication important for Shankhapushpi?
What family does it belong to?
mnemonics: SHANKHA = small spreading herb with trumpet/funnel flower
student.quick_revision: Shankhapushpi — Convolvulus pluricaulis — Convolvulaceae — whole plant — Medhya.

practical_points: Observe habit, leaf shape and flower
Compare authenticated sample with market sample

doctor.quick_reference: Traditionally used as a Medhya drug; botanical authentication is essential.
key_precautions: Do not extrapolate experimental evidence to clinical efficacy
